items.title: opencode-claimant: recovery rule for bound sessions that never received their prompt (#4758)
items.body: Fixes #4758 Phase 3 of design #4912 (claimant session contract): a bound session that never received its prompt previously had no recovery path — not a launch candidate, resend already spent, gone-session rule inapplicable while the empty session existed. **poll.py (read-only discovery)** - New `stuck_bound` output (top-level + per-queue): claimed opencode-lane tasks bound to a root session with no terminal marker (`time.idle`/`outcome`), NOT in the server's active set, silent for at least `ACTIVE_WINDOW_MS` (the existing 30-minute zombie window — one threshold, not two), and with the task's lease expired. Every unknown fails closed (unreadable active set, missing session, unparseable lease all veto). Entries carry `attempts`/`max_attempts` so the claimant can pick the branch. Zero-message verification is deliberately NOT claimed from the session list — the claimant must verify it before acting. - `is_candidate` now accepts stage `launch_failed` alongside `handed_off` as a recorded yield, so a task reclaimed by the recovery rule becomes a launch candidate again instead of being stranded by its own recovery checkpoint. **prompt.md (claimant contract)** - Step 1 gains the recovery rule: verify zero messages (any message/marker/activity vetoes — a live, progressing session is never reclaimed) → DELETE the verified zero-message session per-id FIRST (a failed or unverifiable delete keeps the binding, fail closed) → attempts remain: checkpoint `launch_failed` as the task's worker, clearing `session_id` (explicit null) and keeping the prior id in the audit field `launch_failed_session_id`; attempts exhausted: terminally `fail` with the bound session id in `--execution`. The checkpoint/fail progress record is the notification Tend's fleet-watchdog reads — no new channel. **Tests** — `python3 -m unittest pm-stack/opencode-claimant/test_poll.py`: 36 pass (15 new: stuck-bound classifier vetoes, lease parsing, `launch_failed` candidacy). Live `poll.py` run from this branch emits `stuck_bound` correctly (0 rows at run time). --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

items.title: fix(opencode-claimant): make handed-off tasks actually bind and execute (task 13488)
items.body: The opencode execution lane has never bound a handed-off task through claimant.py: lanes hand off, the claimant fires, and nothing launches. Four defects compounded: - poll.py json-parsed the repo-queue binary's list output, which is a human table since the #5362 cutover, so every queue read as empty and the gate always exited (#7325, #7375). - The checkpoint verb records the yield at progress.last_checkpoint.stage; is_candidate reads progress.stage, so even a working read classified ~0 candidates (#7706). - launch_step never read mode — a shadow fire reaching step 4 would have created and bound sessions (#7366) — and it bound sessions without ever sending the execution prompt, manufacturing #4758 zero-message sessions (#7356). Its session calls also carried none of the server's required Basic auth. - The broker's rich /list (built for this claimant) did not return the task payload, so launch prompts carried an empty packet. Fixes: - poll.py reads claimed rows from the broker's /list with rich: true (URL/token resolved exactly as the fleet client resolves them), lifts the yield stage from last_checkpoint, and exposes payload as the candidate packet. Fail-closed semantics unchanged: an unreadable queue contributes no rows. - claimant.py supervision reads rows through poll.py; launch_step in shadow mode records the would-launch window as skips and mutates nothing; the live launch creates the session with auth, binds it, then delivers the prompt via POST /api/session/{id}/prompt with message-reconcile before any resend, flagging the launch entry when the prompt cannot be landed. Session responses unwrap the v2 data envelope. - fleet-queue: rich /list selects payload on both the Turso and PostgREST paths and parses it as JSON (Turso). Verification (laptop): python suites 60/60 pass (test_poll + test_claimant, incl. new coverage for the broker read, stage lift, payload packet, shadow no-mutation, prompt-failure flagging and prompt reconcile). Live read-only smoke of the fixed poll.py against the production broker: 22 candidates across the queues (was 0 all day), cap_room 35, no poll warnings. Queue task 13488 (the claimant-binding fix task; its packet names #1187, the dispatch design this claimant implements). Fixes #7325 Fixes #7375 Fixes #7366 Fixes #7356 Fixes #7706 --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

items.title: fix(opencode-claimant): read session messages from /message and fail closed on unknown
items.body:
## Defect

`pm-stack/opencode-claimant/claimant.py` read a session's messages from
`GET {OPENCODE_URL}/api/session/<id>/messages` in two places:

- `supervision_step()` — the #4758 "verify zero messages first" guard
  (before deleting a bound session and atomically rebinding its task);
- `_get_messages()` — the reconcile read `_send_prompt()` uses to decide
  whether one resend is allowed.

On the standing laptop OpenCode v2 server that path does not exist: it
returns **HTTP 404 with a zero-byte body**. Both call sites ran curl
*without* `-f` and then `json.loads(stdout or "[]")`, so the 404 parsed
to `[]` — a confirmed "zero messages" that never happened. The correct
endpoint is `GET /api/session/<id>/message`, which returns
`{"data": [ ...messages... ], "cursor": {...}}`.

## Live evidence (2026-11-09, http://127.0.0.1:13420)

Sampled four real sessions from `GET /api/session`:

```
ses_e5e40adbccfffe5tL3Wrx51oUl  /messages 404 (0 bytes)  /message 200  n=100 at limit=100
ses_e5e403fe19cffeWYfpPV90r6Ta  /messages 404 (0 bytes)  /message 200  n=58
ses_e5e3fbfb4a1ffeHj2ReQt5sy1v  /messages 404 (0 bytes)  /message 200  n=17
ses_e5e403fe514ffeSDLSefGjZqEF  /messages 404 (0 bytes)  /message 200  n=89
```

The default page is 20 messages; `?limit=100` returns the counts above,
confirming `/message` really carries the full list. (The task report
encountered 29 and 25 messages for two other sessions; the point is the
same: `/messages` 404s, `/message` 200s with `{"data": [...]}`.)

## Behavioural consequence

1. The supervision guard was **inert**. A gone/idle bound session was
   always judged "zero messages", so the loop could DELETE a session
   that actually had messages and atomically clear its task binding
   (`--launched-by opencode-claimant-recovery:zero-message-deleted`),
   making the task relaunchable — the duplicate-execution defect the
   ordering exists to prevent.
2. `_get_messages()` returned `[]` instead of `None` when the read
   failed, so `_send_prompt()` could POST a second prompt into a session
   whose first prompt may already have landed.

Both docstrings already stated the intended rule: an unreadable session
is **UNKNOWN**, never empty.

## What changed

- Both paths now use `GET /api/session/<id>/message`.
- curl runs with `-f`, so any non-2xx is a failure.
- Strict parsing: only a JSON object with a **list** under `data`
  (unwrapped) or a bare JSON list is a confirmed read. Empty body,
  non-JSON, dict without a list `data`, error object, or transport
  failure returns `None` (UNKNOWN).
- `supervision_step()` now calls `_get_messages()` (one shared
  fail-closed parser) instead of its own curl/parse. `None` leaves the
  task bound — printed as a note, no DELETE, no bind. Only a confirmed
  `[]` enters the zero-message recovery path.
- Added the missing lease guard: a bound task is recoverable only once
  `poll.parse_lease_ms(task.get("lease_until"))` is in the past.
  An unparseable lease is **not** expired.
- No functions renamed, no launch/bind logic changed.

## Tests

`pm-stack/opencode-claimant/test_claimant.py` harness updated to the
`/message` endpoint and given `messages_rc` and a DELETE recorder.
New regression coverage:

- 404 / empty-body read (return code non-zero, and also a 200 with an
  empty body) → no candidate, no DELETE, no bind;
- bound session that HAS messages → not recovered;
- confirmed `{"data": []}`/`[]` → still recovers exactly as before
  (DELETE then `bind ... --launched-by
  opencode-claimant-recovery:zero-message-deleted`), including the
  live 200 shape `{"data": [], "cursor": {}}`;
- bound task with an unexpired lease → not recovered;
- unparseable lease → not recovered.

Commands run (Python 3.14.8 from the user environment; no pytest):

```
python3 -m py_compile pm-stack/opencode-claimant/claimant.py pm-stack/opencode-claimant/test_claimant.py
  -> COMPILE_OK

python3 -m unittest pm-stack/opencode-claimant/test_claimant.py
  -> Ran 15 tests in 0.035s — OK (exit 0)

python3 -m unittest pm-stack/opencode-claimant/test_poll.py
  -> Ran 50 tests in 0.043s — OK (exit 0)
```

`ruff check` on the two files reports 49 findings, all pre-existing
categories (BLE001, PLW1510, UP006/UP035/UP045, DTZ003, EXE001, …); the
repo has no ruff config for this path and CI's format tier is not a
merge gate. No new finding category was introduced.

## Not verified

- I did not run the claimant in live mode against the real queue, so I
  did not observe an actual recovery fire or delete on a production
  session. The change was exercised only through the stubbed transport
  test harness plus the direct live endpoint probes above.
- I did not test a session with exactly zero messages on the live
  server (none was convenient to create); the confirmed-empty shape is
  covered by the unit tests.
- Full repository test suite was not run — only the two claimant suites.

## Open questions / defaults chosen

- Note-only handling for an unknown supervision read (a `print`, not a
  new skip record): supervision's return type is a candidate list and
  `log_fire` is not threaded into it, so recording the skip would be a
  larger change. Default: keep it a note, matching the file's existing
  warning idiom.
- Supervision reuses `_get_messages()` rather than duplicating the
  parser. This is intentional so the two reads can never diverge again.
- Lease expiry uses `time.time()` in milliseconds, matching
  `poll.is_stuck_bound`'s `now_ms` convention.

Refs #3026.

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/leptos-rs/leptos/compare/v0.8.17...v0.8.19)

A patch release, mostly of bugfixes.

Note: one of these includes a behavior change, which is that the primary server function encodings now respect the Axum/Actix request body size limits, rather than ignoring them. If you are accustomed to sending very large data (for example, a POST request > 2mb) via server functions, you may need to increase the request body size limit via Actix `PayloadConfig` or Axum `DefaultBodyLimit` (see docs for each server framework.)

Multipart data (file uploads) are not affected.

### [`v0.8.5`](https://redirect.github.com/leptos-rs/leptos/releases/tag/v0.8.5): : WASM code splitting released!

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/leptos-rs/leptos/compare/v0.8.4...v0.8.5)

This release includes WASM code-splitting/lazy-loading support, in tandem with the latest `cargo-leptos` release.

You can use the [`lazy_routes`](https://redirect.github.com/leptos-rs/leptos/tree/main/examples/lazy_routes) example to understand what this means!

Essentially, though, there are two patterns:

1. Use the `#[lazy]` macro to make any given function lazy
2. Use the `#[lazy_route]` to designate a route with a lazy-loaded view, which is loaded concurrently with the route's data

`#[lazy]` converts a (sync or async) function into a lazy-loaded async function

```rust

#[lazy]
fn deserialize_comments(data: &str) -> Vec<Comment> {
    serde_json::from_str(data).unwrap()
}
```

`#[lazy_route]` lets you split routes into a "data" half and a "view" half, which will be concurrently loaded by the router. This works with nested routing: so if you have ViewD and ViewE, then the router will concurrently load D's data, D's (lazy) view, E's data, and E's (lazy) view, before navigating to the page.

```rust
struct ViewD {
    data: Resource<Result<Vec<i32>, ServerFnError>>,
}

#[lazy_route]
impl LazyRoute for ViewD {
    fn data() -> Self {
        Self {
            data: Resource::new(|| (), |_| d_data()),
        }
    }

    fn view(this: Self) -> AnyView {
        let items = move || {
            Suspend::new(async move {
                this.data
                    .await
                    .unwrap_or_default()
                    .into_iter()
                    .map(|item| view! { <li>{item}</li> })
                    .collect::<Vec<_>>()
            })
        };
        view! {
            <p id="page">"View D"</p>
            <hr/>
            <Suspense fallback=|| view! { <p id="loading">"Loading..."</p> }>
                <ul>{items}</ul>
            </Suspense>
            <Outlet/>
        }
        .into_any()
    }
}

#[server]
async fn d_data() -> Result<Vec<i32>, ServerFnError> {
    tokio::time::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(250)).await;
    Ok(vec![1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13])
}
```
